title: Data models, shared types, and atomic write utility
description:
Create `lib/learn/conventions.py` with the foundational data models and utility functions that all pipeline phases depend on.

Dataclasses to define:
- `RawPattern(type, files, scope, adherence, evidence, observation_support, recent_trend)` — intermediate representation from Phase A/B
- `ConventionEntry(id, convention, scope, confidence, canonical_example, exceptions, evolution, tags, evidence, source)` — final convention record
- `ConventionResult(conventions, conflicts, candidates, meta)` with a `summary()` method that formats CLI output

Utility function `_atomic_write(path: Path, data: dict | list) -> None` — writes JSON to a temp file then renames to prevent partial corruption.

Also define type aliases and constants: confidence level literals (`established`, `emerging`, `decaying`, `conflict`), source literals (`config`, `discovered`), rejection reason literals.

The `__init__.py` at `lib/learn/__init__.py` already exists (confirmed in codebase context). Do not modify it in this task.
acceptance_criteria:
- RawPattern dataclass has fields: type (str), files (list[str]), scope (list[str]), adherence (float), evidence (str), observation_support (int, default 0), recent_trend (str, default 'stable')
  verify_by: schema_check
- ConventionEntry dataclass has fields: id (str), convention (str), scope (list[str]), confidence (str), canonical_example (str), exceptions (str|None), evolution (dict|None), tags (list[str]), evidence (dict), source (str)
  verify_by: schema_check
- ConventionResult dataclass has fields: conventions (list[ConventionEntry]), conflicts (list[dict]), candidates (list[ConventionEntry]), meta (dict)
  verify_by: schema_check
- ConventionResult.summary() returns a string containing convention count, candidate count, and source breakdown
  verify_by: test
- _atomic_write writes to temp file then renames; partial write (simulated interrupt) does not corrupt target file
  verify_by: test
decisions: format_knowledge_for_agent uses backward-compatible field reading: entry.get('knowledge', entry.get('content', entry.get('text', ''))) and entry.get('why_it_matters', entry.get('title', '')). The coherence fix says to use the spec fields (knowledge, why_it_matters), but existing tests in test_convention_pipeline.py (owned by Task 9) use the legacy fields (content, title). Pure spec compliance would break those tests; backward compat satisfies both.
_load_existing_conventions now also reads conflicts from conventions.json['conflicts'] directly, so the loaded result includes persisted conflict data.
_count_observations_at_run() helper added to count total observations and convention_violation observations from the obs_dir JSONL files, feeding the two new required meta fields.
concerns: tests/test_convention_pipeline.py (Task 9) uses title/content fields in test data for format_knowledge_for_agent. Task 9 should update those tests to use knowledge/why_it_matters once the backward-compat period ends.

The views format remains array-of-objects [{id, text, scope}] rather than the spec's string-per-agent format. Changing it would break format_conventions_for_agent's scope-filtering capability. The spec may need updating to match the implementation.
